$comment: Accepted MISSING findings for tools/osm-drift-check.py, keyed by IDENTITY (slug|reason), never by count — a count ratchet stays green when one entry is resolved and another vanishes the same week, which is the event this check exists to catch. Adding a key here is a DECISION: write a note saying why. Removing a facility from the site is a separate, later act.
$adjudication_2026_08_19: The eight entries this file shipped with on 2026-08-19 were adjudicated one at a time under TODO #1228, each against the OSM object's own version history (api.openstreetmap.org/api/0.6/<type>/<id>/history.json), the changeset that made the edit, an Overpass re-query of the surrounding area, and a named second source. NOT ONE of the eight was a closure. Seven were MERGES — a POI node deleted and its tags moved onto the building polygon at the same spot, which is routine OSM housekeeping and looks identical, from an id lookup, to a facility that shut down. One (Elliot Provincial Hospital) was a RETAG of the wrong polygon: in changeset 185535921 the mapper correctly re-identified way:217484563 as Elliot High Hostel on Barry Way and moved the hospital's own tags onto way:461683581 at 1 Maclear Road, so OUR id was wrong and always had been. All eight facility_ids were repointed at the surviving object and their coordinates re-read from it; two of ours were badly wrong (H.A. Grove by 1.3 km, Elliot Provincial by 1.9 km), which on this site is a trip someone cannot afford. Zero records were deleted and no URL changed. The lesson worth keeping: a deleted OSM node is a question, not an answer — six of the seven merges were made by one experienced South African mapper (VisibleSouth, ~6,400 changesets) whose changeset comments name the facility being tidied.
$reconciliation_2026_08_21: THREE NUMBERS, ONE QUESTION, NO CONTRADICTION (#1351/#1363, reconciled 2026-08-21). The clinicfinder keeper reported '4 published facilities no longer exist in OpenStreetMap' (2026-08-19 21:15 SAST), this check reported MISSING 1, and a full Overpass sweep the next day reported 0. All three were true answers, and the disagreement is a TIMELINE plus a MISLABELLED COUNT, not a data defect. (1) THE KEEPER'S 4 WAS CORRECT AND IS NOW STALE. It queried the 517 records then claiming services.emergency_24h using their PRE-#1228 facility_ids. The set of records #1228 repointed INTERSECTED WITH emergency_24h is EXACTLY 4, by name: ha-grove-hospital-mpumalanga (zaf_node_1460687699), tower-psychiatric-hospital-eastern-cape (zaf_node_7896380488), general-justice-gizenga-mpanza-regional-hospital-formerly-stanger-hospital-durba (zaf_node_9048293718) and elliot-provincial-hospital-eastern-cape (zaf_way_217484563). The repoints landed in commit a431ac6 at 22:17 SAST — 62 minutes after the keeper measured them, and eight hours before /site-review-headless filed #1351 from the already-superseded capture at 06:30 the next morning. Nothing was ever left broken. (2) NOT ONE OF THE 4 HAD CLOSED, verified against the OSM API on 2026-08-21. node/1460687699, node/7896380488 and node/9048293718 all answer HTTP 410 GONE: each was a POI node deleted when a mapper merged its tags onto the building polygon at the same spot, the routine housekeeping the 2026-08-19 adjudication found seven times. way/217484563 answers HTTP 200 and is `amenity=school`, name 'Elliot High Hostel' — our id had been on the wrong polygon all along. Whether the keeper's Overpass query filtered on health tags (making Elliot 'not returned') is NOT reproducible from its capture and is deliberately not asserted here; the disposition is identical either way. All four current ids — way:468966258, way:218396423, way:168965151, way:461683581 — answer 200 with amenity=hospital AND healthcare=hospital. (3) THE '1' AND THE '0' ARE THE SAME READING OF DIFFERENT QUESTIONS. This check's MISSING bucket holds two reasons: 'no element returned' and 'no longer tagged healthcare'. Its 1 is the second reason (cambridge-clinic, the accepted entry below) — its own capture records osm_objects_returned equal to the number checked, i.e. it ALSO measured zero elements gone. (4) #1363'S TWO FACTUAL ERRORS, corrected so they are not re-derived. It states the sweep 'returned an element for all 1,076'; the capture data/capture/osm-tags/2026-08-20.json states records 1076 and elements_found 1073. The gap is NOT three absent facilities — it is three pairs of records sharing one OSM object, every one created by #1228's own repointing (way:468966258, way:218396423, way:461683581). Zero records lack an element. It also states all 1,076 'still carry a healthcare key or a health amenity value'; exactly one does not — way:1103021023, amenity=social_facility, which is the MISSING 1. #1362 repeats that second claim as a premise and should be read with this correction. (5) THE RECONCILIATION EXPOSED A REAL COVERAGE HOLE, fixed the same day. parse_ids keyed a dict by OSM id, so the second record on a shared object silently overwrote the first and was never compared — and because the dropped record left the denominator too, the run printed '1073 records checked' when 1073 was the OBJECT count. A finding was genuinely being lost: ha-grove-hospital-mpumalanga carries 'Ha Grove Hospital' against OSM's 'H.A. Grove Hospital' and never appeared in NAME_CHANGED. The check now compares every record and reports records_checked (1076) and osm_objects_checked (1073) separately. THE ANSWER TO THE ORIGINAL QUESTION IS ZERO: no published facility is gone from OSM. Zero records were edited, zero pages removed, zero URLs changed.

accepted.name: Cambridge Clinic (Sprigg Street Clinic)
accepted.note: OSM IS WRONG AND WE ARE RIGHT — the one disposition of the eight where the source, not the record, is the defect. node:2298902321 was deleted in changeset 181516414 ('Cambridge Clinic') and its tags merged onto the building at the corner of Sprigg and Dominion Street, way:1103021023, which carries our exact phone number (+27 43 726 0142). In merging it the mapper reclassified it as amenity=social_facility / social_facility=day_care / operator:type=private, i.e. a private day-care centre. Second source: Medpages lists 'Sprigg Street Clinic' under Clinics - PUBLIC, Cambridge, East London (orgcode 143929), and directory listings put Cambridge Clinic at Cnr Sprigg St & Dominion St, 5247 — the same corner, the same phone, a public primary-care clinic. The facility_id is repointed at way:1103021023 so the guard keeps watching the object that actually exists; this key accepts the classification disagreement rather than the object's absence. Re-adjudicate if the OSM tags change again — the key includes the reason, so a different tag fires afresh.
